given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Loans are lent on 03-02, so dueOn is 03-16, and the clock is set to 03-17 before the job runs.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The database starts empty, so no reminder exists before the first run.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: Asserts that fakeNotifications.sent holds the exact memberId, loanId and dueOn for both loans, and that there are exactly two.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: Queries the reminders table and asserts loan_id and sent_on of 2026-03-17, with a length of 2.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice on the same day, so loan1 already has a reminder the second time.
loan2 is overdue but is returned before the job runs.
The third loan is lent on 03-03, so it is due 03-17, which is today. That is the boundary case.

then.why: toMatchObject on an array also checks its length, so only loan1 is sent, and only once across both runs. A resend, a returned loan or a not-yet-overdue loan would fail it.

given.why: fakeNotifications.refuseFor(loan1) makes the fake return a refused delivery.
B5 maps a failed connection to a refused delivery. The service only ever sees 'refused', so no separate setup is needed here.

then.why: The reminders table is asserted to contain only loan2's row.
Asserts a log entry with level warn and event reminder.failed.
The matcher is objectContaining on level and event only. The fields are never asserted, so logging the wrong id would pass.
The refusal reason 'Notifications API answered 503' is set up but never asserted in the log. A hard-coded error string would pass.

then.part: and carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan1 is lent first and refused, and loan2 must still be sent, so replacing continue with break would fail.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, two accepted and one refused, and the job runs to completion.

then.why: The last log entry is asserted with toEqual on level info, event reminders.finished and fields { sent: 2, failed: 1 }.

given.why: A reminder fixture with memberId, loanId and dueOn is passed to the real client.

then.part: Sends `POST {NOTIFY_URL}/notifications` with JSON `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: Asserts the exact method, path, content-type and body shape on the captured request.
200, 202 and 204 are each asserted as accepted, which defeats a check for 200 only.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 gives kind refused with a reason containing '400'.

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: HttpResponse.error() gives kind refused with a reason containing 'unreachable'.
